name: NY Strip Steak with Shallot-Red Wine Vinegar Sauce & Swiss Chard

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat steak dry with paper towels and cut into portions. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg striploin (New York strip) steak
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add steaks and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate, cover with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)

Meanwhile, wash and dry chard; fold leaves in half lengthwise and, using a clean cutting board, slice off the stems. Cut leaves into bite-sized pieces and thinly slice the stems, keeping them separate. Place leaves in a large bowl, reserving stems for the next step.

Preheat a large pot over medium heat. Once the pot is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chard stems, salt, and pepper to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp butter, unsalted
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add chard leaves to the pot in handfuls, waiting for the leaves to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Wash, dry, and juice lemons into the pot with the chard and stir to combine. Cover and remove from heat.
Peel and slice shallots crosswise into thin rounds.

Return reserved skillet (with steak drippings) to medium heat, add more butter, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shallot and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, 5-6 minutes.
When the shallots are soft, add water, vinegar, and sugar to the skillet. Bring to a simmer and cook until sauce is reduced by half, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup water
⅓ cup red wine vinegar
1 tbsp brown sugar

instructions.primary_message: To serve, divide steaks and lemony chard between plates. Spoon shallot sauce over steaks and enjoy!
